title_en: The Life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
summary: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ﷺ (c. 570–632 CE) is the final Prophet and Messenger of Allah, sent to all of humanity until the Day of Judgment. His life, preserved in the Seerah literature and hadith, is the model for all Muslims. This overview covers the major phases: birth, pre-prophethood, revelation, Meccan period, Hijrah, Madinan period, and his passing.
content:
## Birth and Early Life

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib ﷺ was born in Makkah approximately in the Year of the Elephant (c. 570 CE), in the clan of Banu Hashim of the tribe of Quraysh. His father Abdullah died before his birth; his mother Aminah bint Wahb died when he was six. He was raised by his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib, then — after his grandfather's death — by his uncle Abu Talib.

He was nursed by Halimah al-Sa'diyyah of the tribe of Banu Sa'd. The opening of his chest (sharh al-sadr) is reported in Sahih Muslim (Hadith 162) as occurring during his infancy with his nurse.

Known before prophethood as al-Amin (the Trustworthy) and al-Sadiq (the Truthful), he was respected in Makkah for his character. He worked as a merchant and made trading journeys to Syria. At the age of approximately twenty-five he married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid رضي الله عنها, a wealthy widow of honour who had employed him.

## The First Revelation

At the age of forty, in the year 610 CE, he received the first revelation in the Cave of Hira on the mountain of Nur during the month of Ramadan. The angel Jibril عليه السلام came to him and said 'Iqra' (Read/Recite). The first verses revealed were the opening of Surah al-'Alaq (96:1–5). He returned home trembling; Khadijah رضي الله عنها comforted him and took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, a learned man of the scripture, who confirmed the nature of the revelation.

## The Meccan Period (610–622 CE)

The Prophet ﷺ called the people of Makkah to Islam secretly for three years, then openly. The early Muslims faced intense persecution from the Quraysh. Key events:
- **First emigrants to Abyssinia:** A group of Muslims emigrated to the kingdom of the Negus (Ashama ibn Abjar) who gave them refuge (c. 615 CE)
- **Year of Grief (619 CE):** Khadijah رضي الله عنها died; Abu Talib died. The Prophet ﷺ lost his two greatest protectors.
- **Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj:** The night journey to Jerusalem (al-Aqsa) and ascent through the heavens, during which the five daily prayers were ordained (Surah al-Isra', 17:1; Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3674)
- **Pledges of 'Aqabah:** Agreements with the Ansar from Madinah to support and protect him (621–622 CE)

## The Hijrah (622 CE / 1 AH)

The migration to Madinah marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar. The Prophet ﷺ left Makkah with Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه, hid in the Cave of Thawr for three nights, and arrived in Madinah (then Yathrib) to a jubilant welcome. In Madinah he:
- Established the Masjid al-Nabawi (the Prophet's Mosque)
- Drafted the Constitution of Madinah establishing the rights and responsibilities of all communities
- Established the brotherhood (mu'akhat) between the Muhajirun (emigrants) and the Ansar

## The Madinan Period (622–632 CE)

Key events of the Madinan decade:
- **Battle of Badr (2 AH / 624 CE):** 313 Muslims defeated an army of 1000 Quraysh; decisive early victory
- **Battle of Uhud (3 AH / 625 CE):** Partial setback; the Prophet ﷺ was wounded; 70 Companions martyred including his uncle Hamzah رضي الله عنه
- **Battle of the Trench (Al-Ahzab) (5 AH / 627 CE):** Combined force of 10,000 repelled by the strategy of digging a trench
- **Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH / 628 CE):** Treaty with Quraysh; apparent compromise that Allah called a clear victory
- **Conquest of Makkah (8 AH / 630 CE):** 10,000 Muslims entered Makkah; the Prophet ﷺ granted general amnesty
- **Battle of Hunayn (8 AH / 630 CE):** Victory against Hawazin and Thaqif
- **Farewell Hajj (10 AH / 632 CE):** Final pilgrimage; delivery of the Farewell Sermon at 'Arafah

## His Passing

The Prophet ﷺ passed away on the 12th of Rabi' al-Awwal, 11 AH (8 June 632 CE), in the apartment of 'A'ishah رضي الله عنها in Madinah, at approximately sixty-three years of age. He was buried in the spot where he died, which is now within the Masjid al-Nabawi.

Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه addressed the Muslims: 'Whoever worshipped Muhammad, then Muhammad has died. But whoever worshipped Allah — indeed Allah is Ever-Living and does not die.' (Sahih al-Bukhari, Hadith 3668)
evidence_hadith: Sahih Muslim, Hadith 162 — opening of the chest
